note: Wire strings for the pinned materialized-temporal format check (the :60-rejecting grammar; see format_conformance). Every row is VALID and must round-trip unless it carries `expect_valid: false`, which declares a wire the materialized grammar REJECTS in every target (absent field = valid). Each runner parses into the language's native temporal type and RE-SERIALIZES via the generator-owned serializer (RFC 3339, ORIGINAL OFFSET PRESERVED with +00:00/-00:00 normalized to Z, T/Z uppercased on the parse path, fractional seconds at the value's own precision with trailing zeros trimmed, no fractional part when zero) -- NO TRUNCATION beyond each native type's genuine capacity limit. The compare harness checks the equally-capable materializing set (go, java, py, js-string, js-temporal) emits byte-identical output for each id. Documented divergences: Python truncates sub-microsecond date-time (native us resolution); legacy TS 'Date' (js-date) folds date-time to a UTC instant at millisecond. The leap-second ':60' rows (dt-leap/t-leap) are no longer a prose SKIP: they carry `expect_valid: false`, because the materialized grammar rejects them in all four targets (measured). They flip back to valid only if the `string` opt-out, which would keep the wider :60-accepting grammar, is implemented.
